subject: Clarification: incident notification & limited forensic access - scope and cooperation
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@finsecure.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarification on notification obligations & limited forensic access

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement review we need to confirm the operational interpretation of a couple of DPA clauses related to incident notifications and evidence access. Two specific asks: 

1) Notification window: our DPA requires "prompt notification" and "no later than 72 hours" for incidents that materially affect customer data. We want to understand Redwood's trigger conditions (telemetry vs confirmed exposure) and the typical cadence for a preliminary notice vs a full report. Do you have an example timeline?

2) Limited forensic access: the contract includes a "limited-escrow/forensic access" carveout that allows customers to request read-only snapshots where permitted. We need clarity on the scope (logs, payloads, KV cache snapshots), the process for requesting access, timing to deliver, and how cross-border transfers are handled for EU data.

Attached is a short forensic summary from our SOC team describing the artifacts they'd request. Can you confirm you can provide an initial response within 24 hours acknowledging scope and an ETA? Also please point us to the internal playbooks or template language you use for these events — legal will want to map operational timelines to the DPA redlines.

Appreciate a quick confirmation.

— Ava
Ava Reynolds
Head of Security Operations, FinSecure
ava.reynolds@finsecure.com

Attachments: forensic_summary_20261214.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynsecure@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification on notification obligations & limited forensic access

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the clear list — this is the right time to align expectations. Short answers up front: we can commit to an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and a preliminary notice within 72 hours when the incident meets the DPA thresholds. For limited forensic access we support read-only snapshots of telemetry, request traces, and a scoped export of KV-cache prefixes where available, subject to subprocessor and jurisdiction constraints.

I looped in Marissa (Legal/Privacy ops) and Soojin (Security) to provide the operational matrix and a suggested clause redline. Marissa — can you attach the current incident-notify matrix and the draft DPA language we typically provide for EU customers? Soojin — can you confirm the list of artifacts we can produce and a rough SLA once a request is accepted (target: 5 business days for a scoped export subject to legal checks)?

Ava — I will send a short one-page timeline and the template notice by EOD tomorrow. If you prefer a call, we can set a 30-minute sync with your SOC/legal.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ava Reynolds <ava.reynsecure@finsecure.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification on notification obligations & limited forensic access

Hi all —

Attaching the proposed notify matrix and a redline of the DPA section (see attachments: proposed_notify_matrix.xlsx, dpa_section_redlines.docx). Key operational points summarized below: 

- Trigger definitions:
  • Telemetry alert: internal signal (anomalous telemetry) that requires investigation — preliminary notice within 24–48 hours stating investigation underway.
  • Confirmed exposure (unauthorized access to customer data): preliminary notice within 24 hours; full report within 72 hours after triage where material impact is confirmed.

- Notice cadence and contents: preliminary notice = high-level summary (scope, suspected vector, immediate mitigations, POC). Full report = timeline, scope of affected datasets, root cause (if known), remediation steps, and evidence artifacts available for transfer.

- Forensic access scope & constraints:
  • Scope: request traces (request IDs, timestamps), aggregated telemetry (anonymized where required), retained logs covering the incident window, and KV cache snapshots only when necessary and scoped to affected tokens/tenants. We will NOT provide live access to runtime processes or full system dumps.
  • Delivery SLA: once request is validated and legal checks passed, we target 3–7 business days depending on data volume and export approvals (quicker for narrow scoping).
  • Cross-border: exports containing EU personal data require a lawful basis (contractual DPA + SCCs where applicable) and may require subprocessors' export authorization; if export is not possible, we provide redacted artifacts or in-region review sessions.

- Process:
  1) Customer submits Formal Evidence Request (FER) using our template (link below).
  2) Security evaluates feasibility and scopes artifacts; Legal confirms DPA alignment & any redactions.
  3) Export/forensics executed; delivery via secure transfer (per-customer vault or signed SFTP).

Links: incident template: https://redwood.app/drive/d/incident-template-v2
FER template: https://redwood.app/drive/d/forensic-evidence-request-template

I've included suggested DPA language in the redline that clarifies timelines (acknowledgement 24 hours; preliminary 72 hours for material incidents) and a clause for "limited, scopped forensic access" that emphasizes read-only exports and legal approvals. Happy to take legal redlines.

Attachments: proposed_notify_matrix.xlsx, dpa_section_redlines.docx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@redsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2026 14:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification on notification obligations & limited forensic access

Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks for the thorough breakdown and the templates — this helps a lot. A couple of clarifying notes from our side after an internal review: 

- 72-hour full report: legal will ask for a concession where root cause may take longer; are you open to a two-stage full report (initial technical summary at 72h + final RCA within 14 days) that we can bake into the DPA?

- KV cache snapshots: we understand the sensitivity. For our use-case we only need a bounded prefix related to affected tenant IDs. We appreciate the "in-region review" option if export is blocked; could you include sample redaction rules and an example of the scoped export format?

Action items we propose: 
  • Redwood to share the scoped export example (redacted) and FER template by COB Monday.
  • Agree tentatively on two-stage reporting language; legal will prepare redlines to your doc and send by next Wednesday.
  • Schedule a 30-min sync (SOC + Legal) for Tuesday 11:00 AM CET to walk through the FER and cross-border process.

If you can confirm the Monday / Tuesday items, we will proceed with including the redline in our procurement packet.

Appreciate the collaboration — will be useful to standardize this for other EU customers as well.

— Ava
Ava Reynolds
Head of Security Operations, FinSecure
